correctness.rationale: A labeled one-point type is exactly an admissible downset/upset pair in a Fraïssé-homogeneous poset. The union-support of a downset has a_s possibilities by binomial inversion; each support has \(a_sM_{n-s}-1\) admissible upper sets because exactly the principal downset forbids the unique upset containing S. This proves the count and formal EGF for every n, including \(n=0\). For the asymptotic, splitting \(s=0,1,n-1,n\) and using log2 M(n)~central-binomial plus convexity of central coefficients makes the middle convolution o(M_{n-1}) and yields \(4M_n+2nM_{n-1}+o(nM_{n-1})\). Standalone brute-force check \(n=0\)..4 agrees with 3,6,18,86,808; no infinite claim rests on the finite test.

value.rationale: Boolean cubes are canonical named bases of unbounded width and dimension; their one-point orbit counts are a natural invariant of the generic poset, and arbitrary-base type counting is #P-complete. The explicit transform reduces the whole family to classical Dedekind numbers, while the nontrivial fourfold concentration and first \(2nM_{n-1}\) correction identify how the restricted counting problem grows. It is not merely a handful of numerical cases or a substitution into the earlier two-chain-grid formula: dimensions at least three lie outside the earlier structural recurrences.
